_note: Thomas, 2026-09-06: 'ready to check out the rest of the uk/GB/ireland/scotland and Au' — the Irish part of thin-coverage round 2. Ireland had 7 nodes, all of them the EU price-index -> national-accounts -> HBS chain plus the EDP inventory and an ESS peer review: no balance of payments, no census, no population estimates, no central bank publication and no statistical law. This round mints those and closes the demographic triangle (census -> population and migration estimates -> labour force survey), which was the piece that made the existing CSO nodes hang together. Every url and every evidence_url was raw-verified HTTP 200 before use and every quote read live from the cited URL. cso.ie, irishstatutebook.ie and centralbank.ie all answered a browser-UA curl; nothing was blocked.

reports.title: International Accounts
reports.description: Ireland's quarterly balance of payments, international investment position and external debt release. Source data come from CSO quarterly statutory enterprise surveys conducted under the Statistics (Balance of Payments and Financial Accounts) Order 2016, supplemented since 2008 by data on credit institutions and investment funds collected by the Central Bank of Ireland. The methodology follows the IMF's BPM6 as far as possible.

reports.title: Statistics Act, 1993
reports.description: The Act of the Oireachtas providing for the collection, compilation, extraction and dissemination of official statistics in Ireland. It establishes the Central Statistics Office, the Director General and the National Statistics Board; section 25 empowers the Taoiseach to make Statutory Instruments requiring people to supply information, and sections 26 and 27 let the Director General require completion of forms following such an Order. It is the parent legislation for every CSO survey, the census included.

reports.title: Census of Population
reports.description: Ireland's full enumeration of every person and dwelling on Census Night, conducted by the CSO roughly every five years; Census 2022 was taken on 3 April 2022 and was the 26th census since 1841. It is conducted under the Statistics Act, 1993 together with a Statistics (Census of Population) Order made by the Taoiseach, and serves Ireland's obligations under EU Regulation (EC) No. 763/2008. It provides the benchmark population that CSO household statistics are weighted and revised to.
reports.cadence_note: Roughly every five years. Census 2022 was taken on 3 April 2022, the 26th census since 1841.

reports.title: Population and Migration Estimates
reports.description: Annual CSO release giving the usually resident population of the State at end-April together with estimated immigration, emigration and net migration for the preceding twelve months. The population is estimated by carrying the most recent Census of Population base forward for births, deaths and estimated migration flows; the gross migration flows are estimated principally from the Labour Force Survey. Estimates are revised once definitive census results become available.

reports.title: Quarterly Bulletin
reports.description: The Central Bank of Ireland's quarterly assessment of the Irish economy, containing the Bank's macroeconomic forecasts for output, employment, wages and HICP inflation, plus signed articles and thematic boxes. It records that the permission of the Government was obtained for its use of material compiled by the Central Statistics Office, and its charts and footnotes cite named CSO outputs including the National Accounts and the International Accounts.

_dropped.why: RE-DERIVED AND REFUSED AGAIN 2026-09-06. This round found the GFS Background Notes sentence 'The GDP figures used in this publication are consistent with those in the Annual National Accounts 2024 published on 08 July 2025' and proposed the edge on it. Two things stop it, and the older one is the better one. (1) PLAYBOOK-CORPUS section 7, 2026-08-31: 'consistent with' is a claim about numbers, not a citation — it describes agreement between figures, not a document naming one as the other's input. (2) eu-government-finance-2026-08-28.json already carries this exact pair as `no-document` with a stronger finding: the CSO warns that annual GFS is benchmarked to the EDP notification and 'may not be fully aligned with the Annual National Accounts', which is the opposite of a data dependency. Rule 14 — the older note wins. Recorded here so the next agent does not re-derive it a third time.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. The LFS Q3 2025 Background Notes and the LFS survey background notes both say only that the LFS produces measures 'in accordance with International Labour Organisation (ILO) concepts and definitions' and that 'The primary classification used for the LFS results is the ILO (International Labour Office) labour force classification', plus EU Regulation (EU) 2019/1700. Neither names the ICLS resolution or any ICLS resolution by title — organisation named, artefact not. Same finding and same decision as the UK and Australian labour force surveys this round.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. Quarterly Bulletin Q4 2024 read in full (direct PDF, HTTP 200). It forecasts and discusses the 'Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) for Ireland' and records that Government permission was obtained for its use of 'material compiled by the Central Statistics Office'. It never names the CSO's Consumer Price Index publication: the HICP is the Eurostat-defined index and the CSO reference is agency-level only.

LEAD 2026-09-06. The CSO's ECOICOP ver. 2 methodology note (https://www.cso.ie/en/methods/prices/consumerpriceindex/methodologydocuments/updateofcpihicpclassificationtoecoicopver2/, HTTP 200) states 'The CSO will be adopting ECOICOP ver. 2 as the classification scheme for the Consumer Price Index (CPI) alongside the HICP from January 2026 onwards' and, separately on the same page, that ECOICOP ver. 2 is identical to UN COICOP 2018. The link to the corpus's `un-coicop-2018` node needs both sentences read together, which is a stitch rather than a citation, and this corpus has already declined generic COICOP citations twice (Iran, Iraq, 2026-08-29). Left as a lead: it wants one sentence naming COICOP 2018 as the CPI's classification basis.
